content:
Over the years, Apple has been adding more customisation options to iOS. iOS 16 brought back full lock screen personalisation, iOS 18 introduced icon colour tinting, iOS 26 introduced translucent icons, and iOS 27 brings full-screen Liquid Glass sliders.

The continued expansion of iPhone personalisation is a good thing. Now that you can tint your home screen icons, why not extend this feature across the entire operating system?

iOS 27 hasn't launched yet, so it may be premature to think about what Apple might do in the next software version. That said, I think adding themed app colours beyond light and dark mode would be a logical next step.

Essentially, I want to recreate Material You's design aesthetic on iOS — but based on icon colours rather than wallpapers — though Apple should also offer wallpaper-based options. Apple first introduced the option to match icons to MagSafe case colours last year, and adding this theming system would fit right in with that.

It's worth noting that Apple earlier brought colour theming to its integrated development environment, Xcode, at this year's WWDC. There are plenty of great options there — why not bring that fun to the iPhone? Even the Mac now lets users set system-wide tints for third-party apps.

Summary

Overall, I think bringing colour theming to iOS would be fantastic and another big step toward giving users more customisation.

What do you think about bringing colour theming to iOS and iPadOS? Let us know in the comments.
